notes:
SMB inbound lead — self-serve signup that raised privacy questions early. Primary product interest: hosted API (self-serve).

Key customer profile: mid-sized SaaS support vendor that integrates chat + ticketing. Wants LLM to suggest replies and generate summaries; will send user messages (including potential PII) into API.

Security/privacy pain: legal and security team uncomfortable with unknown retention of prompts and model training usage. Quote from Head of Ops: "We need an ACL: don't keep our prompts longer than X days and give us a way to opt out entirely. Also, how are transcripts logged?"

Technical asks (summary):
- Can Redwood hosted API be configured to not retain prompts or to auto-delete after N days?
- Is there a deletion/opt-out API for stored request logs?
- Are prompts ever used to improve models or for training? Need written guarantee if not retained for training.
- What audit logs are available (request-level, token-level cost)?
- Can we have retention and residency controls for EU customers (future ask)?

Guidance so far provided: shared hosted privacy FAQ and SOC2 docs; indicated hosted_api default does short-term logging for operational/debugging but offers retention controls for customers with explicit requests. Need to confirm SLA and deletion API specifics.

Sales notes: lightweight POC likely if we can offer 30-day retention and opt-out flag. Price sensitivity: SMB budget; ARR estimate modest.
